data.note:
Correctly called DNA replication for methotrexate (PubChem CID 126941, ChEMBL CHEMBL34259 - Dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor, BBBC021 structure verified). ChEMBL mechanism explains BBBC021 "DNA replication" annotation: DHFR inhibition depletes tetrahydrofolate → purine/thymidine synthesis block.

Phenotype observed: profound decrease in DAPI mean (-9 to -11 z) and integrated DNA, with enlarged spread cells (cell_area +5 to +9 z) and near-zero mitotic fraction, already saturated at 0.03 µM, exactly expected for antifolate S-phase cytostasis. Atlas was appropriately cautious: NSC 2/4 DNA replication vs tied 4/10 vs 4/10 neighbours (mean 0.68 vs 0.64) and per-well split across 3 classes, with Microscopist excluding actin/microtubule/Aurora/Eg5 but calling MoA unknown.

Literature supports: Fridland et al. directly showed DNA replication inhibition in methotrexate-treated human lymphoblasts (PMID 1175648), and Wood & Wu review methotrexate/pralatrexate antifolate mechanisms via DHFR (PMID 26433846). Despite PI-noted budget limit preventing requested replicate 2 at 0.03 µM, highest-similarity low-dose vote (0.843) correctly captured the class.

reflection.text:
Unblinded correct: methotrexate e26/e27 PubChem CID126941 DHFR inhibitor, atlas ground truth DNA replication, our conclusion DNA replication p=0.36-0.38 was correct but with appropriately low confidence and a tie that justified the Request Experiment verdict.

What evidence got right: The core quantitative phenoprint was consistent and extreme across all 4 acquired wells despite single replicates: nuc_dna_mean z -11.9 e2 [0.3 uM], -10.1 e3 [10 uM], -9.6 e12 [0.03 uM], -11.7 e13 [1 uM]; cell_area z +7.1 to +9.4 e2/e3/e12/e13; nuc_solidity +4.8 to +8.0 e2/e12; cell_eccentricity -8.5 e13. This saturated pale-DNA / enlarged-cell cytostatic profile with no increase in frac_mitotic_like e17 rho -0.26 p=0.74 correctly argued against Aurora/Eg5/microtubule stabilizer/destabilizer mitotic arrest, which describe_phenotype e5/e6 also excluded by lacking actin/microtubule hallmarks. The mapping of DHFR inhibition to reduced DNA synthesis is directly supported by the unblinding literature: PMID 1175648 DNA replication in methotrexate-treated lymphoblasts and PMID 26433846 Methotrexate and Pralatrexate review.

Atlas comparison did narrow to the right pair but also revealed the tie we correctly did not over-interpret: e4 over 2 wells NSC 1/2 Kinase, k-neighbours 4/10 DNA replication vs 4/10 Kinase; e14/e23 over 4 wells NSC 2/4 DNA replication, k-neighbours 4/10 vs 4/10, mean similarity 0.68 vs 0.64, per-well winners spanning 3 classes. Our rationale to favor DNA replication based on highest per-well similarity at the least toxic low dose e12 0.03 uM [similarity 0.843] and absence of kinase/microtubule discriminating morphology was what allowed a correct call, but update_hypotheses e20/e24 0.38 vs 0.32 and 0.36 vs 0.33 correctly kept it as a near-tie, not a confident call.

What misled / what we missed and why:

1. Measurement interpretation - dose_response: e15 nuc_dna_mean rho -0.20 p=0.8, e16 cell_area rho -0.40 p=0.6, e18 cell_count rho -0.20 p=0.8 were read as 'no dose trend' when they actually reflected saturation already at the lowest acquired dose 0.03 uM e12. That plus conflicting visual density e5 'similar vs DMSO' at 0.3 uM vs e6 'lower vs DMSO' at 10 uM made cytotoxicity/cytostasis ambiguous.

2. Comparison limitation: e5/e6 microscopist explicitly called MoA 'unknown' on only 2 fields each; they excluded obvious microtubule/actin patterns but did not separate DNA replication from kinase inhibition, leaving the atlas tie unresolved. No paper in this run supported the enlarged-cell phenotype specifically - search_literature 'methotrexate cell cycle arrest S phase phenotype' returned 0 hits e29 - so we made that claim without citation, correctly.

3. Acquisition choice: sampling strategy e2 dose 4, e3 dose 7, then e12 dose 2, e13 dose 5 efficiently covered 4 doses but exhausted budget e22 0/4 wells left with only single replicates per dose. This directly prevented the requested reproducibility test - acquire dose index 2 replicate 2 and rerun NSC - that the review correctly flagged as needed to distinguish 0.68 vs 0.64 tie. We flagged budget exhaustion e22/e24 but could not resolve it within this run.

In retrospect the saturated low-dose signal plus tie should have triggered earlier replication rather than a 4th dose point. Correct outcome, correctly low certainty. This is a cell-biology screening interpretation only, not clinical advice.
what_was_right: Extreme consistent nuc_dna_mean z -9.6 to -11.9 and cell_area +5.6 to +9.4 across e2/e3/e12/e13 with low frac_mitotic_like e17 supported G1/S cytostatic DNA replication stress vs mitotic classes correctly excluded by e5/e6
Atlas tie correctly narrowed to DNA replication vs Kinase 4/10 vs 4/10 e14/e23 with low-dose 0.843 similarity vote correctly weighted to top call
DHFR inhibitor identity e26/e27 maps to DNA replication MOA consistent with PMID 1175648 and PMID 26433846
what_was_wrong: Dose_response p=0.8 rho -0.20 e15 misinterpreted as no effect rather than saturation at 0.03uM e12; cell_count e18 and density e5 vs e6 conflict unresolved
Phenotype descriptions e5/e6 on 2 fields each called MoA unknown and did not discriminate DNA replication vs kinase; low hypothesis probabilities 0.38 vs 0.32 e20 kept as tie
Acquisition exhausted 4/4 wells e22 with single replicates preventing requested replicate 2 test, leaving per-well votes spanning 3 classes e23

citations.claim: DNA replication inhibition in methotrexate-treated cells supports atlas mapping of DHFR inhibitor to DNA replication class
Methotrexate annotated as dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor consistent with e26/e27

reflection.next_experiment: Acquire dose index 2 0.03uM replicate 2 and rerun NSC as requested; orthogonal EdU pulse + PI cell cycle + pH2AX/p21 at 0.03 and 0.3uM with reference DNA replication inhibitor control to resolve DNA replication vs kinase tie - not clinical testing.

## Reflection

Unblinded correct: methotrexate e26/e27 PubChem CID126941 DHFR inhibitor, atlas ground truth DNA replication, our conclusion DNA replication p=0.36-0.38 was correct but with appropriately low confidence and a tie that justified the Request Experiment verdict.

What evidence got right: The core quantitative phenoprint was consistent and extreme across all 4 acquired wells despite single replicates: nuc_dna_mean z -11.9 e2 [0.3 uM], -10.1 e3 [10 uM], -9.6 e12 [0.03 uM], -11.7 e13 [1 uM]; cell_area z +7.1 to +9.4 e2/e3/e12/e13; nuc_solidity +4.8 to +8.0 e2/e12; cell_eccentricity -8.5 e13. This saturated pale-DNA / enlarged-cell cytostatic profile with no increase in frac_mitotic_like e17 rho -0.26 p=0.74 correctly argued against Aurora/Eg5/microtubule stabilizer/destabilizer mitotic arrest, which describe_phenotype e5/e6 also excluded by lacking actin/microtubule hallmarks. The mapping of DHFR inhibition to reduced DNA synthesis is directly supported by the unblinding literature: PMID 1175648 DNA replication in methotrexate-treated lymphoblasts and PMID 26433846 Methotrexate and Pralatrexate review.

Atlas comparison did narrow to the right pair but also revealed the tie we correctly did not over-interpret: e4 over 2 wells NSC 1/2 Kinase, k-neighbours 4/10 DNA replication vs 4/10 Kinase; e14/e23 over 4 wells NSC 2/4 DNA replication, k-neighbours 4/10 vs 4/10, mean similarity 0.68 vs 0.64, per-well winners spanning 3 classes. Our rationale to favor DNA replication based on highest per-well similarity at the least toxic low dose e12 0.03 uM [similarity 0.843] and absence of kinase/microtubule discriminating morphology was what allowed a correct call, but update_hypotheses e20/e24 0.38 vs 0.32 and 0.36 vs 0.33 correctly kept it as a near-tie, not a confident call.

What misled / what we missed and why:

1. Measurement interpretation - dose_response: e15 nuc_dna_mean rho -0.20 p=0.8, e16 cell_area rho -0.40 p=0.6, e18 cell_count rho -0.20 p=0.8 were read as 'no dose trend' when they actually reflected saturation already at the lowest acquired dose 0.03 uM e12. That plus conflicting visual density e5 'similar vs DMSO' at 0.3 uM vs e6 'lower vs DMSO' at 10 uM made cytotoxicity/cytostasis ambiguous.

2. Comparison limitation: e5/e6 microscopist explicitly called MoA 'unknown' on only 2 fields each; they excluded obvious microtubule/actin patterns but did not separate DNA replication from kinase inhibition, leaving the atlas tie unresolved. No paper in this run supported the enlarged-cell phenotype specifically - search_literature 'methotrexate cell cycle arrest S phase phenotype' returned 0 hits e29 - so we made that claim without citation, correctly.

3. Acquisition choice: sampling strategy e2 dose 4, e3 dose 7, then e12 dose 2, e13 dose 5 efficiently covered 4 doses but exhausted budget e22 0/4 wells left with only single replicates per dose. This directly prevented the requested reproducibility test - acquire dose index 2 replicate 2 and rerun NSC - that the review correctly flagged as needed to distinguish 0.68 vs 0.64 tie. We flagged budget exhaustion e22/e24 but could not resolve it within this run.

In retrospect the saturated low-dose signal plus tie should have triggered earlier replication rather than a 4th dose point. Correct outcome, correctly low certainty. This is a cell-biology screening interpretation only, not clinical advice.
